title: Zakura recap: security claims in their scope
text:
OPENZCASH
OPERATIONS
ENGINEERING DETAIL
26
Zakura recap: security claims in their scope
November 1 retrospective of October · corroborating engineering and audit publications
598 to 197 Rust dependencies
The team reports 75% smaller binaries and roughly half the
fresh-build time after dependency work.
Adversarial formalization audit
zkSecurity found no bypass within the stated scope; it
identified limitations around assumptions and model
boundaries.
Different CPUs and compilers
ARM64/Cranelift and x86-64/LLVM nodes compare results.
Shared logic bugs can still affect both.
83.2% mining-hashrate adoption
This is the team’s month-end estimate, not an independent
OpenZcash census of node distribution.

title: Zakura recap: network and wallet work
text:
OPENZCASH
OPERATIONS
ENGINEERING DETAIL
27
Zakura recap: network and wallet work
Measured performance, experimental networking and deployment status
Block announcements
Team medians: 833 to 7.5 ms; discovery: 2,255 to 3.2 ms.
Empty-mempool delays over 1 second: 8.2% to 0%.
P2Pv2 resource budgets
Experimental transport adds resource limits and adversarial
simulations. Default on Testnet, not Mainnet.
PIR and address rotation
October work extends private retrieval to Ironwood and
transparent queries, alongside rotation and WOTS demos.
Swaps: integrated, not deployed
One-time incoming viewing keys target quantum linkability of
published swap addresses, through wallet libraries.
